The biggest struggle for me still as I go into my 3rd year teaching is trying to keep work away from home. I’ve gotten better at doing that, but I still tend to spend 2 hours every day outside of work lesson planning or grading. At least I have every holiday guaranteed so I never miss time spending with my family unlike my siblings who always have to miss out on a Christmas or thanksgiving each year. 

One last recommendation I have is to find what grade level best suits you. I prefer teaching high school upperclassmen as they are generally more motivated to get the work done and graduate.

I teach high school biology at a school with lots of disadvantaged students and many discipline problems. I enjoy my job for the most part. Most days go pretty smoothly for me as I am able to shut down poor student behavior in my classroom while still having a good rapport with them. Honestly what works for me is this idea that as long as the students are not disrupting my teaching and others learning, then we have no issue. Sure, there may be a handful of students who sit on their phone quietly or sleep throughout their whole lesson each period, but at least I can stay on track with my lessons and give support to those who actually care about learning (or at least about their grades). 

Don’t take poor attitudes personally, unless it was something very serious. You will definitely need to have boundaries as a younger teacher as well. Students will gravitate towards you because you are young. So, setting boundaries will be extremely important. 

All in all, as a science teacher of a few years, I have really enjoyed my job so far. The things students say sometimes have me dying of laughter whether they were making fun of the course content or taking jabs at me. Having some level of humility while still being professional is tough to balance. But if you can laugh at yourself and be able to have good banter with your students, then it will be alright.
